core.m1: A phone plan is an agreement for mobile service.
core.m2: It can include data, calling, and texting.
core.e1: I need a phone plan with enough data.
core.e2: This phone plan costs fifty dollars each month.
core.p1: I want a _______ with unlimited calling.
core.p2: Which _______ is best for new customers?

core.m1: Prepaid means you pay before using the service.
core.m2: It is flexible because there is usually no contract.
core.e1: I use a prepaid SIM card in Canada.
core.e2: A prepaid plan is good for short stays.
core.p1: I need a _______ plan for one month.

core.m1: A contract is a legal service agreement.
core.m2: Many phone contracts last one or two years.
core.e1: My contract ends next spring.
core.e2: Read the contract before you sign it.
core.p2: I do not want a two-year _______.

core.m1: A carrier is a company that provides phone service.
core.m2: Rogers, Bell, and Telus are common carriers in Canada.
core.e1: Which carrier has good coverage here?
core.e2: My carrier has a store near my home.

core.m1: Monthly cost is the amount you pay each month.
core.m2: Phone plans often show the monthly cost before tax.
core.e1: What is the monthly cost of this plan?
core.e2: The monthly cost is too high for me.
core.p1: What is the _______ of this plan?
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="24" y="14" width="32" height="52" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle cx="40" cy="58" r="3" fill="#C8956C"/><path d="M32 24h16" stroke="#C8956C" stroke-width="1.5"/></svg>

core.m1: Data lets your phone use the internet without WiFi.
core.m2: Phone data is usually measured in gigabytes.
core.e1: My plan includes ten gigabytes of data.
core.e2: I use a lot of data for maps.

core.m1: Unlimited means there is no fixed limit.
core.m2: Some plans include unlimited calling or texting.
core.e1: This plan has unlimited texting.
core.e2: I want unlimited data if possible.

core.m1: Speed tells how fast internet data moves.
core.m2: Internet speed is often measured in Mbps.
core.e1: What internet speed do you recommend?
core.e2: The speed is fast enough for video calls.
core.p1: What _______ do I need for streaming?

core.m1: Download means to receive data from the internet.
core.m2: You download apps, photos, and files to your device.
core.e1: I need to download the carrier app.
core.e2: The download speed is very fast.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><path d="M18 50Q40 28 62 50" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M28 42Q40 32 52 42" fill="none" stroke="#C8956C" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="54" r="5" fill="none" stroke="#8BA888" stroke-width="1.5"/></svg>

core.m1: Upload means to send data to the internet.
core.m2: Video calls and cloud backups need upload speed.
core.e1: My upload speed is ten Mbps.
core.e2: I upload documents for work.
core.p2: I need to _______ photos to the cloud.

core.m1: A router sends WiFi around your home.
core.m2: It connects your devices to the internet.
core.e1: The router is in the living room.
core.e2: Please restart the router first.

core.m1: WiFi is wireless internet for phones and computers.
core.m2: Many homes, cafes, and schools have WiFi.
core.e1: What is the WiFi password?
core.e2: The WiFi is weak in my room.
core.p2: The _______ password is on the wall.

core.m1: A provider is a company that offers a service.
core.m2: Internet and phone providers sell plans to customers.
core.e1: Who is your internet provider?
core.e2: This provider has a good promotion.

core.m1: Installation is the setup of internet service at home.
core.m2: A technician may come to install the modem or router.
core.e1: The installation is next Tuesday.
core.e2: Is installation included in the price?

core.m1: A password is a secret code for access.
core.m2: You need a password to join private WiFi.
core.e1: I forgot my WiFi password.
core.e2: Please write down the password for me.

core.m1: A bill shows how much money you owe.
core.m2: Phone and internet bills usually come every month.
core.e1: My phone bill is sixty dollars.
core.e2: I received my internet bill today.
core.p1: Why is my _______ higher this month?

core.e1: There is a ten-dollar charge on my bill.
core.e2: Why did you charge me twice?

core.m1: Overage is extra usage beyond your plan limit.
core.m2: Data overage can make your bill higher.
core.e1: I paid overage fees last month.
core.e2: Unlimited data helps avoid overage.

core.m1: A discount lowers the price of a service.
core.m2: Students and new customers may get discounts.
core.e1: Do you offer a student discount?
core.e2: This discount lasts for twelve months.
core.p1: Is there a _______ for new customers?

core.m1: A promotion is a special offer for a limited time.
core.m2: Phone stores often advertise promotions for new plans.
core.e1: There is a promotion this month.
core.e2: The promotion includes free installation.
core.p2: This _______ is only for new customers.

core.m1: Coverage is the area where your phone signal works.
core.m2: Good coverage is important outside big cities.
core.e1: Does this carrier have coverage in my area?
core.e2: The coverage is weak in the mountains.
core.p1: How is the _______ in this neighborhood?

core.m2: A weak signal can make calls drop.
core.e1: The signal is poor in the basement.
core.e2: I get a strong signal downtown.
core.p2: Do you have a better _______ outside?

core.m2: Carriers use different networks across Canada.
core.e1: This network is reliable in my city.

extended.m: The amount of data that can move through a connection.
extended.ex: Video streaming needs high bandwidth.

extended.m: High-speed internet service for homes or offices.
extended.ex: We upgraded to broadband internet.

extended.m: A very fast internet technology using light signals.
extended.ex: Fiber optic internet is fast and stable.

extended.m: A device that connects your home to internet service.
extended.ex: Restart your modem if the internet drops.

extended.m: A software program on a phone or computer.
extended.ex: Download the carrier app to check your usage.

extended.m: A mobile package for internet usage.
extended.ex: My data plan renews on the fifteenth.

extended.m: When internet speed is reduced after high usage.
extended.ex: Throttling can happen after you use too much data.

extended.m: Watching video or listening to audio online.
extended.ex: Streaming uses a lot of data.

extended.m: Sharing your phone internet with another device.
extended.ex: I use tethering for my laptop.

extended.m: Using phone service outside your normal network area.
extended.ex: International roaming fees can be expensive.

extended.m: A one-time fee to start a new service.

extended.m: A penalty for ending a contract early.
extended.ex: Ask about the early termination fee before signing.

extended.m: To get a better phone, plan, or service.
extended.ex: I want to upgrade my phone next year.

extended.m: A code used to protect or verify an account.

extended.m: A feature that alerts you during another call.
extended.ex: Call waiting is included in the plan.

extended.m: A system for leaving recorded voice messages.
extended.ex: Leave a voicemail if I do not answer.

extended.m: A system that shows location and directions.
extended.ex: Use GPS to find the store.

extended.m: Wireless technology for connecting nearby devices.
extended.ex: Connect your headphones with Bluetooth.

extended.m: Online storage for files and photos.
extended.ex: Back up your photos to cloud storage.

extended.ex: You need a SIM card for this phone.

extended.m: A digital SIM built into a phone.
extended.ex: Some new phones can use an eSIM.

extended.m: A unit used to measure data amount.

extended.m: A unit used to measure internet speed.

extended.ex: Use strong passwords for cybersecurity.

phrases.en: What phone plans do you have?
phrases.note: Use this when asking a store staff member about options.

phrases.en: I need a plan with enough data.
phrases.zh: 我需要一個有足夠流量的方案。
phrases.note: Use this to explain your main need clearly.
Ask this before choosing a plan or contract.

phrases.en: Are there any promotions right now?
phrases.zh: 現在有任何促銷優惠嗎？
phrases.note: Use this to check whether a better deal is available.

phrases.en: Can you help me troubleshoot my WiFi?
phrases.zh: 你可以幫我排除 WiFi 問題嗎？
phrases.note: Use this when calling tech support or your provider.

dialogues.title: Asking About Phone Plans
dialogues.sit: You are at a phone store and need a new phone plan.
lines: Hi, I need a new phone plan.
Sure. How much data do you need?
I need enough data for maps and video calls.
This plan has twenty gigabytes of data.
It is fifty-five dollars before tax.
No, it is month to month.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask for unlimited data instead.
dialogues.tn: Focus on phone plan, data, monthly cost, and contract.

dialogues.title: Choosing Prepaid or Contract
dialogues.sit: You are comparing prepaid service and a contract plan.
lines: What is the difference between prepaid and contract?
Prepaid means you pay before using the service.
A contract may include a phone discount.
dialogues.tp: Try again: you only stay in Canada for six months.
dialogues.tn: Help the student explain short-term needs clearly.

dialogues.title: Understanding a High Bill
dialogues.sit: Your phone bill is higher than expected.
lines: My bill is higher than last month.
I thought my monthly cost was fifty dollars.
You used extra data this month.
So this is an overage charge?
Yes, the overage charge is fifteen dollars.
Can I avoid this next month?
You can upgrade to a larger data plan.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask the agent to explain an installation charge.
dialogues.tn: This is the required problem scenario. Practice bill, charge, overage.

dialogues.title: Setting Up Home Internet
dialogues.sit: You call an internet provider to set up service at home.
lines: I need home internet for my apartment.
I need good speed for video calls.
Yes, installation is free this month.
We can come next Tuesday morning.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask for a Saturday installation.
dialogues.tn: Practice speed, download, installation, and provider.

dialogues.title: Calling Tech Support
dialogues.sit: Your WiFi is not working at home.
lines: Hi, my WiFi is not working.
I can help you troubleshoot it.
The signal is weak in my bedroom.
Okay. Should I check the password too?
Yes, please confirm the WiFi password.
Great. Call us again if it stops working.
dialogues.tp: Try again: the network is still down after restarting.
dialogues.tn: Practice router, signal, password, network, troubleshoot.

speaking.q: Do you use prepaid or a contract plan?
Do you usually use WiFi or mobile data?
speaking.h: I usually use ___ at home and ___ outside.

speaking.q: Describe your ideal phone plan. Start with: I need a plan with...
speaking.h: Include data, monthly cost, and contract.

speaking.q: Your bill is too high. What would you ask the provider?
speaking.h: Use: Why is my bill ___? What is this charge?

speaking.q: Compare phone plans in Taiwan and Canada. What feels different?
speaking.h: Speak for 30 seconds and give one example.

culture.title: Phone Plans in Canada
culture.photo: 📷 A Canadian phone store with plan posters and SIM card displays.
culture.notes: In Canada, phone and internet plans can feel expensive for newcomers. Many people compare carriers, ask about promotions, and check whether the price is before tax. It is normal to ask direct questions before signing anything.
qs: What carrier do you use now?
Do you prefer prepaid or a contract?
What question would you ask before signing a plan?

culture.title: Reading Bills Carefully
culture.photo: 📷 A phone bill showing monthly cost, taxes, and extra charges.
culture.notes: Canadian bills may include base price, taxes, activation fees, overage charges, or discounts. Many newcomers only look at the total, but it is better to check every line item and ask the provider to explain unclear charges.
qs: Have you ever had a bill higher than expected?
Which charge would you check first?
How can you politely ask for an explanation?

pronunciation.fz: 英文過去式 -ed 的三種發音

words.tip: After a voiced sound, -ed sounds like /d/.

pronunciation.tip: Do not always say -ed as a full extra syllable. Listen to the final sound before -ed.
pronunciation.prac: I asked about the plan, called the provider, and installed the router.
